subject: Clarify SOC 2 coverage: S3 event-time vs ingestion-time and rollforward expectations
messages:
From: Acme Corp Compliance <security@acme.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenfield Audits <audit@greenfieldlp.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 report - clarification on event timestamps and inclusive dates

Hi David,

Thanks again for sending the SOC 2 Type II report. Two quick clarifications from our side before our internal review:

1) The report period in the cover page reads "January 1, 2025 - December 31, 2025". For our ingest pipeline reconciliation we need to confirm whether S3 object event timestamps (the original event_time written by producers) are considered the authoritative "point-in-time" for evidence, or whether Redwood treats the ingestion processing_time (when logs landed in your processing cluster) as the snapshot moment for controls testing.

2) If the auditor relied on point-in-time snapshots, do those snapshots represent end-of-day UTC instants (e.g., 23:59:59 UTC) or do you use processing cutoffs (e.g., when a daily batch job completes)? This matters for some of our cross-system reconciliation.

Could you also provide a short statement (or bridge letter) confirming whether any retroactive backfills or replay windows (Kinesis/S3 replays) were excluded or included in the evidence set?

Appreciate a short note so we can route the answer to our auditors.

Best,
Talia Rosen
Lead Compliance Analyst
Acme Corp

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Corp Compliance <security@acme.com>
Cc: Greenfield Audits <audit@greenfieldlp.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report - clarification on event timestamps and inclusive dates

Talia —

Thanks for the clear questions. Tagging Sergio (Infra) and Marissa (GRC) to confirm and provide the short statement. Quick summary from my side so you have context before the formal reply:

- Our evidence set for 2025 primarily used system-generated snapshots taken by the evidence pipeline at end-of-day UTC.
- Where possible we preserved original producer event_time (S3 object metadata) in logs; those values are retained in the raw log archive but the auditor's control tests were run against the EOD snapshots (the manifests reference ingestion offsets).
- We did perform a small number of backfills for a service migration in March 2025; those backfills are documented and excluded from the auditor's sample population per the exceptions manifest.

Sergio / Marissa — can you confirm wording we can use for Acme and whether Greenfield needs a formal bridge letter or a short confirmation email will suffice? Also attaching the evidence manifest and a redacted log-retention matrix for reference.

Thanks,
David

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_2025_report_stub.pdf (summary), log-retention-matrix.csv

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Compliance <security@acme.com>, Greenfield Audits <audit@greenfieldlp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report - clarification on event timestamps and inclusive dates

Hi all —

Detail from infra ops / evidence lead:

1) Point-of-capture vs. snapshot: we store two timestamp fields for every log/event ingested — producer_event_time (written by the client/producer) and ingestion_time (assigned by the Vector/Fluent Bit collector when the record is received). For SOC 2 evidence the auditors sampled the end-of-day snapshots produced by our evidence pipeline which tie to ingestion offsets. In short: the auditor's control testing used the EOD snapshot (ingestion_time-based snapshot manifest), not the raw event_time stream.

2) End-of-day definition: our EOD snapshots are generated at 00:05 UTC for the preceding UTC day (i.e., snapshot covers 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 UTC by event capture window but the manifest indexes ingestion offsets up to the 00:05 job completion). We do not assert the snapshot as-of an individual millisecond — the manifest contains the ingestion offset range for each service.

3) Backfills/replays: we maintain a replay policy — out-of-bound replays (e.g., Kinesis replays for incident remediation) are recorded and flagged in the evidence manifest. For the 2025 period there were three documented backfill events tied to a March migration; Greenfield excluded those ranges from their sample selection. The backfill tags are available in the attached manifest (redacted).

Suggested wording for Acme (one-paragraph):
"Redwood Inference confirms that for the SOC 2 Type II examination covering Jan 1, 2025 — Dec 31, 2025, auditors tested controls using system-generated end-of-day snapshots produced by our evidence pipeline (snapshot completion ~00:05 UTC for each calendar day). The snapshots are indexed by ingestion offsets; original producer timestamps are retained in the raw archives but were not the primary point-in-time used for auditor control testing. Any documented backfills or replays (e.g., the March 2025 migration) were flagged in the evidence manifest and excluded from the auditor's sample population."

Marissa — is a signed bridge letter on Redwood letterhead required, or will the above paragraph in an email suffice for Acme's audit documentation?

— Sergio

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Corp Compliance <security@acme.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenfield Audits <audit@greenfieldlp.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 report - clarification on event timestamps and inclusive dates

Hi Talia, David, Sergio —

Thanks for the patience. Greenfield confirmed they do not require a formal signed bridge letter in this case; a short signed confirmation on Redwood letterhead is acceptable and we'll include the evidence manifest. Please see the finalized statement below — we will put this on Redwood letterhead and send a PDF by EOD tomorrow:

Final statement (for Acme):
"Redwood Inference confirms that the SOC 2 Type II examination for the period January 1, 2025 — December 31, 2025 utilized system-generated end-of-day snapshots produced by Redwood's evidence pipeline. Snapshots are generated after daily ingestion processing completes (snapshot job finishes at approximately 00:05 UTC) and are indexed by ingestion offsets. Where available, producer_event_time values are retained in raw archives for reconciliation but were not the primary timestamp used for auditors' control testing. Documented replays/backfills (notably the March 2025 migration backfills) were captured, labeled in the evidence manifest, and excluded from the auditor's testing sample population."

If your auditors would like, Greenfield can append a short addendum explaining their sample exclusion criteria; otherwise this confirmation should satisfy cross-system reconciliation needs."
